questions.question: What does CC stand for in email?
questions.explanation: CC stands for Carbon Copy. It is used to send a copy of the email to additional recipients, and all recipients can see who is in the CC field.

questions.question: BCC recipients in an email are visible to ___.
questions.explanation: BCC stands for Blind Carbon Copy. BCC recipients are hidden from all other recipients — only the sender knows who was added in the BCC field.

questions.question: SMTP is used to ___.
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used for sending emails from a client to a server and between mail servers.

questions.question: POP3 is used to ___.
questions.explanation: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) is used to download and receive emails from the mail server to your local device.

questions.question: What is the maximum attachment size in Gmail?
questions.explanation: Gmail allows attachments up to 25 MB in size. If the file is larger than 25 MB, Gmail automatically uses Google Drive to share the file.

questions.question: Emails that have been composed but not yet sent are stored in the ___ folder.
questions.explanation: Unsent or incomplete emails are automatically saved in the Drafts folder. You can open them later to continue editing and send.

questions.question: The @ symbol in an email address separates ___.
questions.explanation: The @ (at) symbol separates the username (local part) from the domain name in an email address. For example, in rahul@gmail.com, 'rahul' is the username and 'gmail.com' is the domain.

questions.question: Which protocol keeps emails on the server and syncs them across multiple devices?
questions.explanation: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) keeps emails stored on the server and synchronizes them across all devices. This is why the same emails appear on your phone, laptop, and tablet.

questions.question: Typing in ALL CAPITALS on the internet is considered as ___.
questions.explanation: In netiquette (internet etiquette), typing in ALL CAPS is considered as SHOUTING. It is considered rude and should be avoided in emails and online messages.

questions.question: What is the full form of SMTP?
questions.explanation: SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol. It is the standard protocol used for sending emails across the internet.

questions.question: Sent emails are automatically stored in the ___ folder.
questions.explanation: When you send an email, a copy is automatically saved in the Sent Mail (or Sent) folder. This serves as a record of all emails you have sent.

questions.question: What is phishing?
options: Fake emails designed to steal personal information
questions.explanation: Phishing is a cyber attack where criminals send fake emails pretending to be from trusted organizations (like banks) to trick recipients into revealing personal information such as passwords, PINs, or bank details.

questions.question: In Gmail, deleted emails are permanently removed after ___ days.
questions.explanation: In Gmail, emails moved to the Trash folder are automatically and permanently deleted after 30 days. Similarly, spam emails are also auto-deleted after 30 days.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid email address?
questions.explanation: Every valid email address must contain exactly one @ symbol separating the username from the domain. 'sneha gmail.com' is missing the @ symbol, making it an invalid email address.

questions.question: Netiquette refers to ___.
options: Internet etiquette or rules of polite online behavior
questions.explanation: Netiquette is short for Network Etiquette (or Internet Etiquette). It refers to the informal rules and guidelines for polite and respectful behavior when communicating on the internet.
